annotations.title: Make a PDF from JPG and PNG images

description: Make a PDF from JPG and PNG images: one image per page, in the order given. Each image is an https:// URL or a data:image/jpeg;base64,… or data:image/png;base64,… URI (this hosted server cannot read local file paths); the type is detected from the bytes, not the name. At most 100 images, each up to 4 MB, 4.5 MB in total. A JPEG's EXIF orientation is applied, so phone photos come out upright. Animated PNGs, other formats (GIF, WebP, HEIC, TIFF, SVG) and PDFs are rejected. Page size, orientation, margin and decoding details are in the arguments. Very large images fail with image_too_large, and many large PNGs in one call with images_too_large_together. Deterministic: the same images give byte-identical output. pdf_merge joins images with existing PDFs. Returns the PDF inline as an application/pdf resource.

image_paths.description: In order, one page each: an https:// URL or a data:image/jpeg;base64,… / data:image/png;base64,… URI (this hosted server cannot read local file paths). PNG: 8-bit and 16-bit, palette, grey, interlaced and transparent files work (transparency is kept); over 10 megapixels fails with image_too_large. JPEG: baseline and progressive, grey, RGB and Adobe-style CMYK; over 250 megapixels fails with image_too_large.

margin.description: Points, 0-200. Default 0 for fit (the page grows by the margin on every side), 36 for a4 and letter.

orientation.description: a4 and letter only; auto (default) picks portrait or landscape per image.

page_size.description: fit (default): page = image size at 72 dpi (1 px = 1 pt; pages longer than 5,000 pt on a side are scaled down, tiny images are enlarged to a 3 pt minimum). a4 or letter: standard page, image centred, shrunk to fit inside the margin and never enlarged.

name: pdf_image_to_pdf

bytes.description: Size of the produced PDF in bytes

resource_uri.description: pdfops:// uri of the inline application/pdf resource
